## Exercise 1

```{r exercise1}
savings <- 0
income <- 58000
interest_rate <- 0.06
savings_rate <- 0.10

for(year in 22:65){
  savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate) + income * savings_rate
}

print(savings)
```

The savings are high because of compound interest. Our money earns interest every year, so it grows faster over time.

## Exercise 2

```{r exercise2}
retirement_income <- savings * 0.04

print(retirement_income)
```

The annual retirement income is about $46,344. It is less than our annual salary of $58,000.

## Exercise 4

```{r exercise4}
savings <- 0
income <- 58000
interest_rate <- 0.06
savings_rate <- 0.10
employer_rate <- 0.05

for(year in 22:65){
  savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate) + income * (savings_rate + employer_rate)
  income <- income + 1000
}

print(savings)

retirement_income <- savings * 0.04
print(retirement_income)
```

## Exercise 5

### Late Saving (Ages 56-65)

```{r exercise5_late}
savings <- 0
income <- 58000
interest_rate <- 0.06

for(year in 22:65){
  if(year >= 56){
    savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate) + income * 0.20
  } else {
    savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate)
  }
  income <- income + 1000
}

late_savings <- savings
print(late_savings)
```

### Early Saving (Ages 22-31)

```{r exercise5_early}
savings <- 0
income <- 58000
interest_rate <- 0.06

for(year in 22:65){
  if(year <= 31){
    savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate) + income * 0.10
  } else {
    savings <- savings * (1 + interest_rate)
  }
  income <- income + 1000
}

early_savings <- savings
print(early_savings)
```

### Comparison

Early saving is better than late saving. This is because compound interest helps our money grow over time. Starting early gives our savings more time to grow.
